theory.intro: The graph of $y=\dfrac{k}{x}$, with $k\ne 0$, is a **hyperbolic curve** that never touches either axis. When $k>0$ and $x>0$, it falls as $x$ increases and comes closer and closer to the axes without touching them. Direct variation, $y=kx$, gives a **straight line through the origin** instead.
facts: An inverse variation graph with $k\ne 0$ is a **curve**, never a straight line.

When $k>0$ and $x>0$, the curve **decreases** from left to right. Negative constants are also possible; an inverse variation graph is not always decreasing. The full hyperbola has two branches, but contexts involving positive quantities use only the positive branch.
steps: Decide whether the graph is a straight line or a curve.
If it is a straight line, check whether it passes through the origin.

For $k>0$ and $x>0$, a decreasing curve approaching both axes without touching them could represent inverse variation. These features alone do not prove inverse variation; when values are available, check that $xy=k$ is constant for all pairs.

workedExamples.solution_text:
A: Direct variation. It is a straight line through the origin.

B: Possible inverse variation. It has the decreasing hyperbolic shape of $y=\frac{k}{x}$ for $k>0$ and $x>0$, approaching both axes without touching them. To confirm inverse variation from values, check that $xy$ is constant.

C: Neither. The straight line misses the origin, and inverse variation requires a curve.

D: Neither. Although it decreases and becomes flatter, it meets the $y$-axis. An inverse variation graph with $k\ne0$ never touches either axis.

workedExamples.question_text:
The model $s=\frac{420}{t}$ gives the average speed $s$ in km/h needed to complete a $420$ km journey in $t$ hours.

Explain why the graph has no point with:

a. $t=0$

b. $s=0$

Explain why only the positive branch is relevant to this journey.
workedExamples.solution_text:
a. At $t=0$, $\frac{420}{0}$ is undefined. Completing a $420$ km journey in zero hours is impossible at any finite speed.

b. At $s=0$, the vehicle does not move and cannot complete the journey in any finite time. For every positive finite $t$, $\frac{420}{t}>0$.

Time and average speed for this journey are positive, so only the positive branch is relevant. The graph approaches both axes without touching them.

foundation.question_text:
The reciprocal model $s=\dfrac{300}{t}$ gives the average speed $s$ (km/h) needed to travel $300$ km in time $t$ (hours).
Explain why $t=0$ and $s=0$ are impossible by referring to the context of the model.
foundation.solution_text:
If $t=0$, then $s=\dfrac{300}{0}$ is undefined. A car cannot travel $300$ km in zero hours at any finite speed.
If $s=0$, the car does not move, so it cannot complete the $300$ km trip in any finite time. For every positive finite time $t$, $\dfrac{300}{t}>0$.
